title: VertexSurge: Variable Length Graph Pattern Match on Billion-edge Graphs
problem: Current graph databases optimized for single-hop subgraph matching fail to efficiently handle Variable-Length Graph Pattern Matching (VLGPM), which requires identifying patterns where the connecting edges between matched vertices have variable lengths.
motivation: VLGPM is essential for analyzing complex dynamic networks like social networks and financial transaction networks where relationship structures vary extensively in both length and connectivity patterns.
method: VertexSurge addresses billion-edge graph pattern matching by specializing beyond single-hop subgraph matching constraints. The system enables efficient traversal and matching of patterns where vertices connect through variable numbers of edges, accommodating the complexity of real-world network topologies.
key_novelty: A scalable system architecture specifically designed to handle variable-length graph patterns on billion-edge graphs, overcoming the single-hop matching limitations of existing graph databases.
contributions: VertexSurge system for efficient variable-length graph pattern matching on billion-scale graphs
Support for patterns with variable edge distances between vertices
Scalable approach for complex network analysis in social and financial domains
limitations: Specific limitations and performance trade-offs not discussed in abstract.
